lead.title: NVIDIA invests in Doctolib to speed up its healthcare AI models, with stronger European infrastructure
lead.deck: Amount undisclosed: the money funds AI hiring and the development of open-weight models, clinical decision support assistants and a personal health assistant in the patient app. Doctolib works with more than 40,000 GPs in Europe and is expanding its European infrastructure over the coming months.

milestone.company: North West London Acute Provider Group
milestone.title: North West London: ambient voice tender for 2027-2030 and a shift from automation to an AI programme
milestone.summary: The group is preparing a three-year AVT contract (1 April 2027 to 31 March 2030), has opened supplier engagement, is moving from RPA to a broader AI programme (strategic outline case and governance paper in preparation), and runs a referral management and discharge planning application from the Federated Data Platform across its four trusts.
milestone.why: A four-hospital buyer is fixing timeline and term ahead of the tender: a clear window for AI scribe vendors, and proof that the FDP is becoming an application layer.

brefsEurope.title: Ligence (Lithuania): CE-marked cardiac ultrasound AI, with a second FDA 510(k) clearance in April 2026
brefsEurope.summary: Its Ligence Heart software plugs into existing imaging systems and reportedly cuts the exam and report from about 30 to 15 minutes; the second clearance adds automated left ventricular strain analysis. The same Tech.eu feature cites Checkpoint Care (Bulgaria), wearable-based remote monitoring that has supported more than 95,000 acute patients.

brefsEurope.title: Magic Vision raises €600K (SixS, business angels) for Silver Eye, its wearable-free AI monitoring for older adults
brefsEurope.summary: Sensors and edge AI detect falls and behaviour changes without storing images; more than 200 sensors installed with Italian care providers, aiming to monitor over 100 people by end-2026 ahead of a further round.

brefsEurope.title: Clatterbridge: ambient voice and Copilot first, plus a trusted research environment to link clinical, imaging and molecular data
brefsEurope.summary: AVT scale-up depends on clinical capacity and safety controls; the shared Liverpool patient record is rated red in the board assurance framework for lack of scope decisions.

brefsEurope.title: Christie, Clatterbridge and Lancashire Teaching publish a five-year radiotherapy strategy built on data and AI
brefsEurope.summary: A working group will set regional data standards and an AI evaluation framework (clinical safety, data quality, post-deployment monitoring); the ambition is to become a "national vanguard" for data-driven radiotherapy.

brefsEurope.title: Wales: only a quarter of health organisations are mostly electronic, an HTN survey finds
brefsEurope.summary: More than half are preparing to leave paper, and a third estimate clinicians lose over ten hours a week to paper; the Welsh Clinical Portal shows nearly 2 million documents accessed per month. Survey sponsored by Altera Digital Health.

brefsIntl.title: US finalises the HTI-5 rule: 14 certification criteria removed, FHIR APIs prioritised
brefsIntl.summary: Model-card requirements for AI decision support are dropped; the rule projects $1.55B in compliance savings and signals read/write FHIR APIs as the future priority.

brefsIntl.title: Wrapped Health raises $2.1M pre-seed (Lightbank, Arteria Capital) to link clinical recommendations to health purchases
brefsIntl.summary: Integrated with EHRs, the platform lets patients buy recommended products using FSA/HSA funds; available via the athenahealth Marketplace.

word.definition: Devices worn or installed at the patient's home measure vital signs and send them to the care team, who can act without waiting for an appointment.

how.t: The patient uses the device at home; the reading travels over the internet or mobile network to the cloud.
The platform flags out-of-range vitals to clinicians.
The clinician assesses the data and gives recommendations or instructions, sometimes after hospital discharge.

word.why: VC angle: remote monitoring frees beds and follows chronic disease outside the hospital; it is software regulated as a medical device (like Hope Care), sold to public health systems with recurring revenue.

startups.name: Hope Care
startups.use: Medical device software for remote monitoring; €6M Series A led by Iberis Capital, used by 15 Portuguese local health units (~45% of NHS users).

startups.name: Checkpoint Care
startups.use: Wearable-based remote monitoring with AI decision support; over 95,000 acute patients supported, 16.5M data points a month.

startups.name: Doccla
startups.use: Virtual ward services for the NHS; £35M Series B led by Lakestar (2024).
